With HRV trends you can learn your health level changes. A up hill trend means a better physical fitness level and a down hill indicates you should pay more attention to your overall health. 5. Generate PDF report with HRV info
6. Send your ECG report to your healthcare provider

So what is HRV?
HRV is a measure of your autonomic nervous system that is widely considered one of the best objective metrics for physical fitness and determining your body’s readiness to perform.

Although HRV manifests as a function of your heart rate, it actually originates from your nervous system. Your autonomic nervous system, which controls the involuntary aspects of your physiology, has two branches, parasympathetic (deactivating) and sympathetic (activating).

The parasympathetic branch (often referred to as “rest and digest”) handles inputs from internal organs, like digestion or your fingernails and hair growing. It causes a decrease in heart rate. The sympathetic branch (often called “fight or flight”) reflects responses to things like stress and exercise, and increases your heart rate.

Heart rate variability comes from these two competing branches simultaneously sending signals to your heart. If your nervous system is balanced, your heart is constantly being told to beat slower by your parasympathetic system, and beat faster by your sympathetic system. This causes a fluctuation in your heart rate: HRV.

Designed by people with ADHD to address our specific executive function challenges, Addie is not just another organizer, productivity or routine planner app. It works with the ADHD brain and all its quirks, strengths and challenges to help you get stuff done.
 
- Overwhelmed by your to-do list? Addie shows you one task at a time in a swipeable, user-friendly interface.
- Don’t know where to start? Addie helps you prioritise your tasks based on their urgency and importance, and crucially for people with ADHD, fun!
- Struggling with motivation? Addie’s gamification engine rewards you for completing tasks to keep the dopamine flowing and your motivation high. Unlock new features and achievements!
- Time blindness making you overcommit or procrastinate? Addie keeps track of how long your tasks take you, so you know for next time. Beat your best time for added motivation!
- Can’t focus? Full-screen tasks with ambient sounds minimise distractions and help you focus on what matters.
- Addie learns what works for you. Better at boring tasks in the morning? Always skip
 
Addie is packed full with these ADHD-specific tools, features and more. Set a mindfulness bell to bring you back to the moment as often as you need it. Use the routine planner and set recurring tasks to support habit building and automate regular tasks.
 
For those important tasks that can’t be ignored, ‘super notifications’ will cut through the noise and grab your focus, so you can feel reassured that Addie won’t let you forget the things that matter.
 
- Get to know your ADHD - 
 
Addie can help you learn more about what works for you. Track your medication, mood, menstrual cycle, and more, to identify trends, understand your physical and mental health and discover what makes you most productive.
 
ADHD diagnosis and treatment are inaccessible for many people. Whether you are diagnosed or not, Addie is a practical solution that can have a significant impact on your life.
 
- Our Founders Story - 
 
Addie Founder, Jo Vickers, had always struggled with things that others seemed to take for granted: focus, organization, motivation and keeping a daily routine.
 
All this took a toll on her mental health, and she tried every routine planner, organizer, productivity tool, focus app and motivation techniques she could find, but nothing stuck.
 
When Jo was late-diagnosed with ADHD, she realised that traditional planners and productivity apps didn’t work with ADHD brains. Their long lists of tasks overwhelmed her, they relied on her to order tasks, and maybe most importantly, they were boring!
 
Taking one problem at a time, she worked to find technology solutions that would work with the ADHD brain, and help people like her overcome their issues with focus, productivity and motivation.
 
Jo worked with the support of the ADHD Foundation and a team of clinical professionals, to bring Addie to life as the ADHD app that is truly designed for people with ADHD.
 
- New Features - 

The Addie team is busy working on more amazing features that will help people with ADHD live a fuller, happier and more productive life. Here’s a sneak preview of what’s coming:
 
- Addie Duo - link two accounts to share tasks, delegate and compete!
- Addie Buddies - buddy up with other users for accountability sessions
- Addie Chat - chat to Addie to braindump, clear your mind and talk through
- Coaching - work with a coach for regular sessions, or occasional accountability check-ins
- Rewards - unlock and enjoy new rewards, including packs of tasks to learn new skills, support your mental health, tackle goals and focus on your personal development
